Olivia (Eng-Infra): heads-up: multiple customers reporting p95/p99 spikes for hosted text-generation since ~2026-02-10 01:20 UTC. Graphs show p95 jumping from ~120ms -> ~450ms and p99 up to ~2.3s on several europe-north nodes. Root suspects: infra churn last night (GPU driver/CUDA updates + kernel pkg roll). opening thread to troubleshoot and coordinate.

Sarah (Support): customer Anshul escalated, repro attached: steady 200 rps, sequence length ~512, tail latency straight up. They saw errors? no, just long responses. They've downgraded batch size to 1 and still see p99 ~1.9s. Customer wants ETA.

James (SRE): any deploys/driver upgrades around that window? I see a host kernel update on 2026-02-10 01:12 UTC and NVIDIA driver 535.14 pushed to a subset of nodes at 01:15 via deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: deploy: gpu-node-image:driver-535.14 -> europe-north-west-01 @ 2026-02-10T01:15:12Z :rocket:

Kai (Runtime): interesting. we pushed a CUDA library update in the same batch (cuda-12.2). runtime metrics show increased CPU softirq on affected hosts at same time. Could be NVMe interrupt storm or driver-level change triggering host I/O stalls while kernel preempts d_tq handling for inference threads.

James (SRE): can we get iostat / dstat / top snapshots from a hit host? wondering if NVMe latency or CPU saturation correlates.

Olivia (Eng-Infra): pulled quick stats from node nvme-3: (snip)

# iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.3   10.1  3072.0  256.0     26.6     2.89    18.9   0.55  66.5
nvme1n1          12.1    1.2   128.0   12.0     11.2     0.02     1.4   0.80   1.2

and top shows ksoftirqd consuming 35-40% CPU spikes when p99 goes up.

# cat /proc/interrupts | grep nvme
48:  1432140  ...  NVMe0
49:   10234  ...  NVMe1

Kai (Runtime): that pattern screams IRQ imbalance. With driver 535 we've seen complaints in other orgs where MSI-X interrupts migrated and caused core hot-spotting. If softirq/irq handling steals cycles from inference threads we get tail latency.

James (SRE): quick mitigation we can try: 1) change scheduler on hot NVMe device to mq-deadline -> none? 2) pin interrupts across cores or set irqbalance policy. Also try reducing queue depth: echo 128 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests (test only). Any objections? low-risk.

Olivia (Eng-Infra): rolling a quick test on a single affected host now: commands I'm running:

echo none > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler
echo 128 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests
systemctl stop irqbalance
for i in $(pgrep -f ksoftirqd); do taskset -pc 0,1 $i; done

Sarah (Support): keeping customer updated: told them we are doing infra-level mitigation tests on a host and will report back within 30m :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

Anshul (Customer Success): customer appreciates the transparency. They asked if it's tied to driver. we need a clear repro so we can sustain a rollback if needed.

James (SRE): after applying scheduler->none + nr_requests=128 on host nvme-3, p99 dropped from ~2.1s to ~220ms within 90s. p95 back to ~140ms. This is promising. Reverting the two sysfs changes returns p99 to ~2s.

Kai (Runtime): good signal. can we get a controlled repro we can run in staging to confirm? steps I propose:
1) provision test node with driver 535 + cuda-12.2
2) run a sustained inference load: wrk-like harness -> 500 rps, seq_len 1024, concurrency 24
3) concurrently run fio randomrw on nvme0n1 with iops=80k, bs=4k, iodepth=32
4) measure tail latency and cpu softirq.

Olivia (Eng-Infra): creating staging job now. also capturing perf samples and nvme reset logs. adding kernel parameter toggles for testing: irqhack=1 (internal name), but really we'll tune RPS/affinity via

echo 1 > /proc/irq/48/smp_affinity
# or use irqbalance --oneshot

James (SRE): also check driver dmesg for nvme reset/recovery lines. I saw a few "nvme: timeout, resetting controller" messages on one host earlier.

Olivia (Eng-Infra): dmesg snippet below:

[  456.789012] nvme nvme0: Abort submission queue failed, escalating to reset.
[  456.789210] nvme 0000:3b:00.0: resetting controller
[  457.012345] nvme nvme0: reset successful

Kai (Runtime): resets would block IO and spike latencies. combined with heavy softirq handling, inference threads waiting on NVMe or scheduler locks see tail latency. This matches customer observations.

James (SRE): what's the rollback plan? We can revert driver to 530 across the fleet, but that's a heavier change. Alternatively we can apply the temporary kernel tuning cluster-wide (scheduler->none, pin IRQs) while we investigate with vendor.

Olivia (Eng-Infra): immediate plan: (A) apply IRQ affinity and queue depth reduction to the affected region as a mitigation; (B) open an NVIDIA support ticket referencing reset logs and kernel version; (C) run staging repro to validate. I'll schedule cluster change in next 10m for europe-north hosts only.
